subject: physics

moments.title: Hertzsprung and Russell plot stars
moments.body: Hertzsprung in 1905-07 and Russell in 1913 plot stars on a diagram with temperature on one axis and luminosity on the other. Most stars fall on a diagonal 'main sequence'. Outliers are giants and dwarfs.
moments.takeaway: A simple scatter plot reveals the entire life cycle of stars.

moments.title: Payne and stellar composition
moments.body: Cecilia Payne, in her PhD thesis, applies Saha's ionisation theory to stellar spectra and concludes stars are overwhelmingly hydrogen and helium — not iron, as everyone thought. Russell tells her the result is 'clearly impossible' and she must add caveats. Four years later he reaches the same conclusion and is widely credited.
moments.takeaway: A 25-year-old woman solves stellar composition — and is overridden by her male advisor.

moments.title: Chandrasekhar limit
moments.who: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar, on a boat to England
moments.body: On the steamship from Madras to England, 19-year-old Chandrasekhar calculates that a white dwarf cannot exceed about 1.4 solar masses without collapsing. At Cambridge, Arthur Eddington publicly ridicules the result. Chandrasekhar receives the Nobel 53 years later, in 1983.
moments.takeaway: The most important stellar limit in astrophysics, derived on a steamship voyage.

moments.title: B^2FH paper
moments.who: Margaret Burbidge, Geoffrey Burbidge, Fowler, Hoyle
moments.body: The 'B^2FH' paper shows how every element heavier than helium is synthesised inside stars and supernovae. Carbon, iron, gold — all forged in stellar nucleosynthesis. Fowler wins the 1983 Nobel; Hoyle, who coined the term 'Big Bang' (originally as mockery), is omitted.

quote.text: We are made of star stuff.

moments.takeaway: Atoms in your body were forged inside dying stars.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Gaia (ESA) has mapped 1.8 billion stars in 3D. JWST resolves stellar populations across cosmic time. The Sun will leave the main sequence in ~5 billion years and become a red giant, then a white dwarf.
now.open_questions: What is the supernova explosion mechanism?

reflection: Cecilia Payne's correct result was dismissed by her senior male colleagues. How does science correct such errors?
